findings.issue_text: db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:31 — embed_category` is deleted unconditionally, but rows are only inserted when `embeddable_hosts` was non-blank; a site that used feed polling (`Jobs::PollFeed` -> `TopicEmbed.import_remote` -> `import`) with an `embed_category` but no `embeddable_hosts` loses its category mapping entirely and silently begins filing every imported topic under a nil category, because `TopicEmbed.import` now derives the category solely from a matching `embeddable_hosts` row.

spec/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller_spec.rb:5 — Both new controller specs assert only `Controller < Admin::AdminController`, i.e. that the file parses and the constant resolves; no request is ever issued, so the routes, `AdminConstraint`, param handling, serializer wiring, and the nil-record 500 paths are entirely unverified, and there is no `spec/models/embeddable_host_spec.rb` at all, leaving `record_for_host`, the host regex, and the nil-host crash with zero coverage — a green CI run here proves essentially nothing about the feature.

app/models/embeddable_host.rb:17 — where("lower(host) = ?", host)` lowercases the column but never the argument, so a referer whose host has any uppercase character (`http://EvilTrout.com/x`) fails to match a row that was stored lowercase and the embed is denied; rows are matched case-insensitively while referers are matched case-sensitively, and `TopicEmbed.import` accidentally avoids this only because it pre-downcases via `normalize_url`.

app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb:10 — update` and `destroy` fetch with `.first` and immediately call `host.host =` / `host.destroy` on a possibly-nil record, so any stale id (two admins in two tabs, or a replayed request) yields a `NoMethodError` 500 instead of a 404; in the delete case the JS `.then` never fires, so the row remains on screen and the admin believes the delete failed to take when it may already be gone.

app/models/embeddable_host.rb:2 — The TLD pattern `[a-z]{2,5}` rejects `.technology`/`.software`-class TLDs, punycode labels containing digits (`xn--p1ai`), `localhost`, and bare IPs, so those sites cannot be added through the UI; worse, the migration bypasses validation entirely, so such rows can exist in the DB and then fail to save the moment an admin edits them.

db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:25 — The INSERT is built by string interpolation of an admin-controlled site-setting value, so a single quote anywhere in the old `embeddable_hosts` setting aborts the migration mid-deploy (after the table was already created with `force: true`) and is a straightforward SQL injection sink.

app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb:9 — update` ignores the request body completely and re-renders the current state with 200 OK — a PUT that reports success while persisting nothing; `saveChanges` in admin-embedding.js.es6 calls it via `embedding.update({})` yet no template wires a button to that action, so the endpoint ships as a dead, silently-lying write API.

app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:61 — Deploy ordering is unsafe in both directions: `ensure_embeddable` and `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` query `embeddable_hosts` on every embed request, so shipping code before the migration turns every embed into a `PG::UndefinedTable` 500 instead of a 403, while running the migration before the restart deletes the `embeddable_hosts` site setting out from under the old code and silently 403s every embed for the length of the window.

db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:3 — create_table ..., force: true` will silently DROP an existing `embeddable_hosts` table and all its rows if the migration is ever re-run or replayed, and `change` containing `execute` is irreversible, so `db:rollback` raises `IrreversibleMigration` — there is no recovery path once the site settings on line 31 have been deleted.

app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb:9 — PUT /admin/customize/embedding` ignores the request body entirely and re-renders the serialized embedding, so the endpoint returns a success shape implying the payload was persisted when nothing is saved (the client's `saveChanges` calls `embedding.update({})` against it).

app/models/topic_embed.rb:43 — category: eh.try(:category_id)` is nil whenever the imported URL's host has no `embeddable_hosts` row (notably RSS/feed-polling imports, which are not host-gated), so those topics now land in uncategorized where `SiteSetting.embed_category` used to apply globally

db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:25 — The host value is string-interpolated straight into SQL (`VALUES ('#{h}', ...)`) with no quoting: a single apostrophe in the stored setting text breaks the statement and aborts the migration, and since the value is admin-supplied free text this is SQL injection executing as the database owner — use `quote(h)`/a bind parameter.

spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb:1 — The contents of the two fabricator files are swapped: `category_fabricator.rb` now defines `Fabricator(:embeddable_host)` while `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` defines the category/diff_category/happy_category/private_category fabricators, breaking the `<model>_fabricator.rb` naming convention used by every other file in that directory and making these definitions unfindable.

app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb:15 — fetch_embedding` invents a fake singleton resource as an `OpenStruct` with a hardcoded `id: 'default'` and no persistence, and `update` renders the serializer without applying any change - a placeholder abstraction that ships a live PUT route (config/routes.rb:139) doing nothing.

app/serializers/embeddable_host_serializer.rb:4 — The explicit `id`, `host` and `category_id` methods only re-delegate to `object` and are exactly what `attributes :id, :host, :category_id` already generates; same redundancy for `id` in app/serializers/embedding_serializer.rb:5.

spec/controllers/admin/embedding_controller_spec.rb:5 — Both new controller specs only assert `< Admin::AdminController`, exercising none of `show`/`update`/`create`/`destroy`; they add file count without coverage and give a false signal that the new endpoints are tested (same in spec/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller_spec.rb).

app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:61 — The embed allowlist check switched from an in-process-cached SiteSetting read (zero DB round-trips) to an uncached `EmbeddableHost` query executed in `ensure_embeddable` for every action, including `/embed/count` which fires on every page view of every embedding site, adding a DB query to the highest-volume public embed path with no caching layer.

app/models/embeddable_host.rb:17 — where("lower(host) = ?", host)` is non-sargable and the migration creates no index on `embeddable_hosts.host` at all, so every embed request and every `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` call does a sequential scan; adding a plain index later would not help without a matching `lower(host)` expression index.

app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb:16 — EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` can return nil and `destroy` (and `update` -> `save_host` at line 10) immediately calls methods on it, so a stale/duplicate delete or any bad id yields a NoMethodError 500 instead of a 404; combined with the un-caught client promise the admin sees nothing happen.

app/models/embeddable_host.rb:6 — self.host.sub!` raises NoMethodError when host is nil (create/update with a missing or null `host` param), turning what should be a format-validation failure into a 500; `save_host` compounds this by dereferencing `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` with no presence check.

app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6:46 — destroyRecord().then(...)` has no `.catch`, unlike `save()` right above it, so a failed DELETE (e.g. the 500 from the nil host above) becomes an unhandled rejection: the row stays in the table and the admin gets no error feedback at all.

app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb:10 — update` persists nothing yet re-renders the serialized object as a success, so `saveChanges` -> `embedding.update({})` in admin-embedding.js.es6 always reports success for a no-op write; that controller action also has no `.catch`, so any real failure is an unhandled rejection.

db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:25 — Migration writes the old setting lines verbatim, bypassing EmbeddableHost's `before_validation` scheme/path stripping, so pre-existing entries like `http://discourse.org` or `https://example.com/1234` are stored with the scheme and can never equal `URI(referer).host` in `record_for_host`; the old `SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host?` explicitly stripped `https?://`, so embedding silently stops working after upgrade (specs miss this because the fabricator goes through the model callback)

spec/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller_spec.rb:5 — The only test asserts `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController < Admin::AdminController`, a tautology guaranteed by the class definition line, so create/update/destroy, params handling and authz are wholly untested; it passes even though `update`/`destroy` call `nil.host=`/`nil.destroy` for an unknown or already-deleted id (500) and `create` with a blank host hits `self.host.sub!` on nil in EmbeddableHost's before_validation (500 instead of a validation error).

app/models/embeddable_host.rb:17 — The new EmbeddableHost model ships with no spec at all (no spec/models/embeddable_host_spec.rb added), leaving `record_for_host`, `host_allowed?`, the scheme/path-stripping before_validation and the format validation untested; e.g. `where("lower(host) = ?", host)` never downcases the parameter, so a referer of `http://EvilTrout.com` fails to match a stored `eviltrout.com` and embedding silently breaks.

spec/controllers/admin/embedding_controller_spec.rb:5 — Same tautological subclass-only assertion, so the endpoint backing the new admin Embedding screen is untested; a request spec would immediately expose that `Admin::EmbeddingController#update` (PUT /admin/customize/embedding, invoked by the UI's `saveChanges`) persists nothing yet renders a success payload.

spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:13 — The "raises an error with a missing host" test no longer establishes any state after `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts = nil` was deleted; with no referer stubbed it now fails inside `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?(nil)` and is an exact duplicate of the "raises an error with no referer" test at line 34, so nothing verifies that an empty embeddable_hosts table blocks embedding.

The migration `20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb` always executes `DELETE FROM site_settings WHERE name IN ('embeddable_hosts', 'embed_category')` even when `embeddable_hosts` is blank and therefore no `embeddable_hosts` rows are created. So a site that previously relied on `embed_category` as a global/default category (without any allowed hosts configured) will lose that setting during migration and, going forward, imports will not apply the prior category (because there will be no matching `EmbeddableHost` row), changing behavior and losing configuration.

In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb the migration reads the old site setting `embeddable_hosts`, splits it into `h`, and then executes raw SQL built via string interpolation: `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, ...)"`. If any `h` contains a single quote, the SQL becomes syntactically invalid and the migration can fail mid-run (after `create_table ... force: true` has already executed). Because the value is injected directly into SQL without escaping/quoting, it is also a SQL injection sink (even if the source is an admin-controlled setting).

On the client side, `admin-embedding.js.es6` defines an action `saveChanges()` that calls `this.get('embedding').update({})`, but the new `embedding.hbs` template only wires `addHost` and per-host save/delete via the `embeddable-host` component—there is no button or action hookup for `saveChanges`. The diff changes embed host checks from SiteSetting-based logic to DB-backed `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?` (see `app/controllers/embed_controller.rb` and `lib/topic_retriever.rb`). `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?` calls `record_for_host`, which executes `where(...)` on the new `embeddable_hosts` table (`app/models/embeddable_host.rb`). If the app code is deployed before running the migration that creates `embeddable_hosts` (`db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb`), requests will hit that query and can raise `PG::UndefinedTable`. Conversely, the migration deletes the old `embeddable_hosts`/`embed_category` site settings rows; running it before restarting onto the new code leaves old code with `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts` blank, causing the old `ensure_embeddable` path (pre-diff) to reject all embeds. adjudication_records.issue_text: db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:3 — create_table ..., force: true` will silently DROP an existing `embeddable_hosts` table and all its rows if the migration is ever re-run or replayed, and `change` containing `execute` is irreversible, so `db:rollback` raises `IrreversibleMigration` — there is no recovery path once the site settings on line 31 have been deleted.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb` the migration uses `create_table :embeddable_hosts, force: true`, which will drop and recreate the table if it already exists (data loss) when the migration is re-applied (e.g., during `db:reset` or if the migration is replayed on a DB that already has that table). More importantly, the migration is written as a `change` method but contains multiple raw `execute` statements (data copy + deletes), which Rails cannot automatically reverse; rolling back will raise `ActiveRecord::IrreversibleMigration`, and the final `DELETE FROM site_settings ...` permanently removes the original settings with no rollback path in this migration.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb:9 — PUT /admin/customize/embedding` ignores the request body entirely and re-renders the serialized embedding, so the endpoint returns a success shape implying the payload was persisted when nothing is saved (the client's `saveChanges` calls `embedding.update({})` against it).

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb`, the `update` action (used by the newly added `PUT /admin/customize/embedding` route) does not read any params or perform any mutation/persistence; it simply re-renders `@embedding` via `EmbeddingSerializer`. Since `@embedding` is an `OpenStruct` built in `fetch_embedding`, there is nothing to save, and any request body is effectively ignored. On the client side, `admin/controllers/admin-embedding.js.es6` defines `saveChanges()` which calls `this.get('embedding').update({})` against this endpoint, so a successful response would misleadingly look like an update occurred even though nothing is persisted.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:61 — The embed allowlist check switched from an in-process-cached SiteSetting read (zero DB round-trips) to an uncached `EmbeddableHost` query executed in `ensure_embeddable` for every action, including `/embed/count` which fires on every page view of every embedding site, adding a DB query to the highest-volume public embed path with no caching layer.

No caching layer is introduced in `EmbeddableHost` in this diff. Therefore, any request path that triggers `ensure_embeddable` now incurs a DB lookup where previously the allowlist check was derived from an in-memory SiteSetting value (no per-request AR query). The finding’s specific mention of `/embed/count` being called on every page view can’t be fully verified from the shown snippet (we can’t see the controller filters/actions wiring here), but the core performance regression (DB query per `ensure_embeddable` call) is directly verifiable in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb:16 — EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` can return nil and `destroy` (and `update` -> `save_host` at line 10) immediately calls methods on it, so a stale/duplicate delete or any bad id yields a NoMethodError 500 instead of a 404; combined with the un-caught client promise the admin sees nothing happen.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController`, both `update` and `destroy` fetch the record via `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` and then immediately call methods on it (`save_host(host)` which does `host.host = ...`, and `host.destroy`). If an invalid/stale `:id` is provided, `first` returns `nil`, leading to a `NoMethodError` and a 500 instead of a 404/handled error. This is directly verifiable from the diff. Additionally, the Ember component’s `delete()` action calls `destroyRecord().then(...)` without a `.catch(...)`, so a server error would result in no user-visible error handling (unlike `save()` which has `.catch(popupAjaxError)`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6:46 — destroyRecord().then(...)` has no `.catch`, unlike `save()` right above it, so a failed DELETE (e.g. the 500 from the nil host above) becomes an unhandled rejection: the row stays in the table and the admin gets no error feedback at all.

If the DELETE request fails/rejects, the rejection is not handled in this code path and the UI removal (`deleteHost`) only happens on success, so the row will remain and the admin gets no error feedback from this component.

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/store.js.es6:192 — _hydrateEmbedded` was broadened from `/(.+)\_id$/` to `/(.+)\_id(s?)$/` with no JS test added, changing hydration for every model that has any `*_ids` attribute, not just embeddable hosts; the new plural branch deletes the `*_ids` key unconditionally and stores the mapped array even when `_lookupSubType` returns undefined for some ids (and the `hydrated || []` guard is dead since `.map` always returns an array).

adjudication.rationale: The diff in `store.js.es6` broadens `_hydrateEmbedded` to match both `*_id` and `*_ids` via `/(.+)\_id(s?)$/`. In the new plural branch it always does `obj[k].map(...)`, assigns the result to `obj[self.pluralize(subType)]`, and then `delete obj[k]` unconditionally. This means for any payload containing `foo_ids`, the raw ids are always removed even if `_lookupSubType` can’t resolve some ids from `root`, producing arrays containing `undefined` entries (no filtering/compaction). Also, `hydrated || []` is effectively pointless because `.map` returns an array whenever it runs, so it won’t fall back to `[]`. This is a real behavioral change affecting all models with `*_ids` keys, not just the new embedding feature, and can lead to incorrect hydration output.
